slides.text: Look, it is not my fault that Swedish furniture names sound identical to ancient Aramaic summoning curses. I was three hours into assembling a six-door wardrobe, muttering the product name—'KVÄnum BRÖmst'—under my breath while bleeding from an Allen-wrench blister, when the living room rug burst into brimstone. A nine-foot horned warlord materialized between my particleboard panels, roaring, 'WHO DARES BIND MALAKOR THE UNYIELDING?'

I blinked through the sulfur smoke and held up page fourteen of the instruction manual. 'Unless you know where the little wooden dowels go, Malakor, step off the veneer. It scratches.' The demon froze. Apparently, because my blood had dripped onto step seven of the diagram during the incantation, the laws of the underworld legally bound him to complete the task in progress before claiming my mortal soul.

By midnight, Malakor the Unyielding was on his knees, weeping black fire. 'Why are there three cam-locks left over?!' he shrieked, shaking a tiny plastic bag at the ceiling. 'The schematic clearly showed twelve!' I handed him a chamomile tea and patted his scaly shoulder. He eventually got the doors aligned, though the left hinge still squeaks whenever someone sins in the hallway.
